fields.Participants: Receiving Clerk, Quality Inspector, LP Officer
fields.Trigger: Inbound receipt of serialized products (power tools, high-value electrical, premium fixtures)
fields.Volume: ~500 SKUs requiring serialization across power tools, premium electrical, appliances

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-scan of "scans vendor serial numbers/QR codes during goods receipt" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-document of "System registers each serial number in authentication database" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-record of "records origin vendor, PO reference, and receipt date" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **Vendor non-compliance**: Some vendors don't provide advance serialization data
- **Manual entry errors**: Typing serial numbers manually introduces data quality issues
System Touchpoints: - Serial number scanning at goods receipt
- Authentication database with vendor ASN matching

steps.activity: Receiving Clerk scans vendor serial numbers/QR codes during goods receipt; system validates against vendor master serialization file (ASN); flags units with missing, duplicate, or non-matching serial numbers for investigation

System registers each serial number in authentication database: vendor, model, manufacturing date, batch/lot, import documentation reference; generates BuildRight authentication QR label applied to packaging

For products without vendor serialization (local brands): system generates BuildRight-unique serial at GR; records origin vendor, PO reference, and receipt date; enables full chain-of-custody tracking from receipt to sale

fields.Participants: IT App Manager, LP Manager, Vendors
fields.Trigger: Customer or staff scans product QR code

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-scan of "scan validation API, mobile-responsive result page, analytics backend" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-validate of "validates code authenticity, returns product information" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-count of "IT generates weekly authentication analytics" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-442 (ensure controlled execution — Product Authentication & Serialization (PA-71.1).)

- operational: unique per-unit codes and geographic scan anomaly detection; authentication-platform uptime SLA monitored (99.9% target) with offline-verification fallback and vendor-API failover tested quarterly
Pain Points / Risks: - **QR cloning**: Sophisticated counterfeiters may copy valid QR codes; mitigated by unique per-unit codes and geographic scan anomaly detection
- **System downtime**: Authentication platform unavailability prevents customer verification
Time Estimate: - ~2–3 hours/week of analytics and platform-maintenance events (per step 3); platform uptime is a continuous SLA, not per-occurrence effort

steps.activity: IT maintains authentication platform: QR code generation engine, scan validation API, mobile-responsive result page, analytics backend; ensures 99.9% uptime for customer-facing verification; manages vendor API integrations for real-time validation

When QR scanned: system validates code authenticity, returns product information (brand, model, manufacturing date, authorized retailer confirmation, warranty status); flags previously scanned codes (potential counterfeiting indicator) for LP investigation

IT generates weekly authentication analytics: scan volume by product category and region, authentication failure rate, geographic scan patterns, repeat-scan alerts (same code scanned at different locations = counterfeiting indicator)

fields.Participants: Customer Service Rep, LP Officer, Category Manager, Vendor
fields.Trigger: Customer reports suspected counterfeit product or requests verification

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-scan of "scan result, purchase receipt, reason for suspicion" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "LP Officer reviews case" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-document of "documents all interactions" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-442 (ensure controlled execution — Product Authentication & Serialization (PA-71.1).)
- operational: Customer Service Representative review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Customer frustration**: Genuine product quality issues misidentified as counterfeiting by customer
- **Evidence collection**: Customer reluctance to provide detailed information or return suspected item
System Touchpoints: - Product image comparison against reference library

steps.activity: Customer submits verification request: product photos, QR code scan result, purchase receipt, reason for suspicion (poor quality, packaging differences, performance issues); Customer Service logs in authentication case system

LP Officer reviews case: compares product images against authentic reference library, validates serial number in database, checks purchase history for source store verification; if counterfeit confirmed: escalates to LP Manager and initiates investigation (W2559)

Customer Service communicates result: if authentic — reassures customer and explains verification; if counterfeit — offers replacement with genuine product, issues refund, requests customer cooperation in investigation (source information); documents all interactions

fields.Frequency: Annual per vendor; ad-hoc for incidents
fields.Trigger: Annual vendor audit cycle or serialization non-compliance incident

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-review of "reviews vendor serialization compliance rate" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-inspect of "inspects suspect vendor products for authenticity indicators" (replaces manual Step 2).
Controls: - CTL-442 (ensure controlled execution — Product Authentication & Serialization (PA-71.1).)
- operational: LP Manager review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Vendor resistance**: Smaller/local vendors lack serialization capability; require technology assistance
- **Cost allocation**: Serialization infrastructure cost passed to BuildRight through higher prices
System Touchpoints: - Vendor compliance dashboard with serialization metrics

steps.activity: LP Manager reviews vendor serialization compliance rate: percentage of shipments with complete ASN serialization data, serial number format consistency, QR code quality, packaging integrity; identifies non-compliant vendors

For non-compliant vendors: Procurement conducts vendor meeting to communicate requirements, timeline for compliance, and consequences (shipment rejection, vendor scorecard impact); Quality inspects suspect vendor products for authenticity indicators

LP Manager establishes serialization compliance as vendor scorecard KPI (minimum 95% compliance); includes in vendor contracts; quarterly review of compliance trends; persistent non-compliance triggers vendor review and potential replacement

fields.Participants: IT Data Architect, LP Manager, IT Operations
fields.Trigger: Platform maintenance cycle or system update

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-scan of "scan analytics, reference image library" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-count of "counterfeit pattern detection" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-record of "IT manages data lifecycle" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - operational: periodic reconciliation against source documents
Pain Points / Risks: - **Data growth**: Serial number database grows ~100K records/month; requires scalable architecture
- **Integration complexity**: Multiple vendor ASN formats and systems
System Touchpoints: - Authentication database with vendor integration APIs
- Analytics and ML platform for pattern detection

steps.activity: IT maintains authentication data platform: serial number database, vendor ASN integration APIs, QR code generation engine, scan analytics, reference image library; ensures data integrity with daily reconciliation against inventory records

IT implements platform enhancements: batch QR code generation for faster GR processing, mobile app integration for in-store verification by staff, vendor self-service portal for ASN submission, machine learning model for counterfeit pattern detection

IT manages data lifecycle: archives sold/expired product serial records (10-year retention per BIR), purges invalid scan data, maintains platform performance targets (<3 sec scan response), manages database capacity growth (~2,000–3,000 new serials/month per W2550; ~500K+ records accumulated over the 10-year BIR retention window)

fields.Participants: LP Analyst, LP Manager, Category Manager, Legal
fields.Trigger: Anomalous scan patterns or market monitoring alerts

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-scan of "LP Analyst monitors for gray market indicators" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-compile of "compiles evidence dossier" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-escalate of "escalates confirmed gray market cases" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-442 (ensure controlled execution — Product Authentication & Serialization (PA-71.1).)
- operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **Online marketplace proliferation**: Difficult to monitor all online channels
- **Internal collusion**: Store staff purchasing discounted products for resale
System Touchpoints: - Scan analytics with geographic anomaly detection
- Online marketplace monitoring (Shopee, Lazada, FB Marketplace)

steps.activity: LP Analyst monitors for gray market indicators: BuildRight-serialized products found in unauthorized retail channels (online marketplaces, competitor stores), geographic scan anomalies (products scanning far from authorized store), bulk scan patterns (reseller activity detection)

Analyst investigates suspicious patterns: traces product origin through serial chain-of-custody, identifies purchase point (store/POS transaction), determines if diversion occurred at vendor, DC, or store level; compiles evidence dossier

LP Manager escalates confirmed gray market cases: to Category Manager for vendor discussion (if vendor-side diversion), to Legal for contractual enforcement, to LP team for store-level investigation (if internal diversion); implements controls: quantity limits for high-risk products, enhanced tracking for repeat offenders

fields.Participants: Category Mgr, Vendor, LP Manager, Merchandising
fields.Trigger: New product introduction or packaging redesign

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-review of "reviews and approves" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-scan of "scannable, label placement per specification, packaging security features" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-442 (ensure controlled execution — Product Authentication & Serialization (PA-71.1).)
- operational: Category Manager review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Packaging redesign cost**: Vendor pushes back on serialization requirements citing cost
- **Label degradation**: QR codes fade or damage during transit, reducing scannability
System Touchpoints: - Product master with serialization requirements per SKU
- GR inspection checklist with serialization compliance item

steps.activity: Category Manager defines serialization requirements per product category: power tools (mandatory vendor serialization + BuildRight QR), electrical components (mandatory for circuit breakers, wiring), appliances (mandatory serial + extended warranty QR), accessories (optional based on price point)

Vendor implements serialization standards: provides specification for QR placement on packaging, data format for ASN transmission, minimum label durability requirements (must survive Philippine humidity and handling); BuildRight LP reviews and approves

Quality Inspector verifies packaging compliance during incoming inspection: QR code present and scannable, label placement per specification, packaging security features (tamper-evident seals, holograms for premium products); non-compliant shipments quarantined until resolved

fields.Frequency: Annual certification; onboarding for new hires
fields.Participants: Training Mgr, LP Manager, Category Manager
fields.Trigger: New hire onboarding or annual refresher
fields.Volume: ~800–1,000 staff in receiving, customer service, and sales roles

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-scan of "scanning procedures, counterfeit identification techniques" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-count of "counterfeit sample comparison for key brands" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-distribute of "distributes via LMS and store communication system" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-442 (ensure controlled execution — Product Authentication & Serialization (PA-71.1).)
- operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **Counterfeit evolution**: Counterfeiters improve quality continuously; training materials must be updated frequently
- **Staff engagement**: Authentication training seen as low-priority vs. sales training
System Touchpoints: - Counterfeit reference library accessible via store mobile app

steps.activity: Training Manager develops authentication curriculum: product authentication fundamentals, QR code scanning procedures, counterfeit identification techniques (visual, weight, packaging quality), escalation procedures for suspected counterfeits, customer communication scripts

Delivery: online module (2 hours) covering identification techniques and procedures; in-store practical workshop (2 hours) with authentic vs. counterfeit sample comparison for key brands (Bosch, Makita, DeWalt, Schneider Electric); certification quiz (90% pass rate)

LP Manager conducts monthly counterfeit awareness updates: new counterfeiting trends, specific brand alerts from vendors, recent investigation outcomes; distributes via LMS and store communication system
